newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-INTER DETERMINED TO ACHIEVE MORE UEFA CUP GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER DETERMINED TO ACHIEVE MORE UEFA CUP GLORY.

text.p: Favourites Internazionale will not let their strong serie A position weaken their resolve to add a third UEFA Cup in the 1990s when they meet Anderlecht in the first leg of the quarter-finals on Tuesday.

Inter, winners in 1991 and 1994, consolidated their second place in the Italian league with a 3-0 win over Piacenza at the weekend, keeping them in line for a place in next season's European Champions' League.

The Belgian side, reeling from match-fixing allegations last month surrounding a 1984 UEFA Cup semifinal against Nottingham Forest, are particularly concerned at having to face England international Paul Ince, who has recovered from a thigh injury.
"I had hoped that Paul Ince would not be fit. He only trained for the first time on Wednesday and still scored twice on Saturday," Anderlecht coach Johan Boskamp said.

Inter should win, but Inter striker Maurizio Ganz warned: "Anderlecht are a very young side and they'll place a lot of emphasis on an aggressive game. They'll chase us around a lot and we'd better be ready."
Ganz is likely to partner Youri Djorkaeff of France in the Inter attack with Ince, Argentine Javier Zanetti, Swiss Ciriaco Sforza and Nicola Berti in midfield.
Boskamp said he would field a five-man defence and only one striker, although Nigerian international Celestine Babayaro is doubtful with a leg injury.

Newcastle manager Kenny Dalglish has bigger strike problems with the prospect of possibly having to make do without 28.5 million pounds ($46.3 million) of talent up front when his side face French league leaders Monaco.

Les Ferdinand is doubtful after pulling a hamstring in the 1-0 home defeat by Southampton on Saturday. His England strike partner Alan Shearer is out after a groin operation, while Colombia's Faustino Asprilla is suspended.
David Ginola, who replaced Ferdinand, seems certain to start against his countrymen and Steve Watson, who has played up front before, could do so again if required.
Newcastle beat French opponents Metz in the previous round, but Monaco have won all their away legs this season.

Monaco have a surfeit of strikers and Nigeria's Victor Ikpeba, who has already scored five goals in the competition, will probably start on the bench with three-goal Brazilian Anderson partnered by teenager prodigy Thierry Henry.
Coach Jean Tigana said: "One of the keys of the match will be to know how to respond to the aerial battle.
"We must not let ourselves be dominated at set pieces and long crosses in front of goal," he added after giving goalkeeper Fabien Barthez intense practice handling centres.
Spain's Tenerife and Valencia had contrasting fortunes in their weekend matches before facing Brondy of Denmark at home and Germany's Schalke away respectively.
Valencia continued to disappoint in a 2-1 loss at struggling Logrones.
Spanish international keeper Andoni Zubizarreta, who will be replaced by reserve Jorge Bartual, and defender Patxi Ferreira are suspended.
Also missing for Valencia will be injured defender Javi Navarro, club captain Francisco Camarasa and Croatian striker Goran Vlaovic.
Schalke, who will be playing in front of a sell-out 56,800 crowd, are desperate to reach their first European semifinal since 1970.
"We'd even shed blood to get there," Schalke's Dutch striker Youri Mulder said.
Coach Huub Stevens must do without inspirational defender Johan de Kock, who is suspended, while Belgian striker Marc Wilmots is doubtful with back problems.
Tenerife have midfielder Pavel Hapal injured and winger Julio Llorente suspended.
Brondby are at full strength, including Peter Moeller who is the top scorer in the UEFA Cup with six goals, and undaunted by Tenerife's rout of Barcelona.

"Barcelona let Tenerife counter attack most of the time, which they do effectively. Barcelona were reduced to nine players for most of the second half. You cannot judge Tenerife from Saturday's match," manager Ebbe Skovdahl said.
